reason: The text explicitly states in Exodus 19:6 that Israel will be 'a kingdom of priests and a holy nation' (ממלכת כהנים וגוי קדוש), indicating that priestly status is conferred upon the entire nation collectively, not upon an elite separate class. The passage does not establish priests as a distinct, superior group with special importance in society. Rather, it democratizes priestly function across all of Israel. The narrative itself portrays Moses as the primary mediator and leader, while Aaron (who performs priestly functions) is shown as capable of error in the golden calf incident, further contradicting any notion of priestly superiority.
